E1.evidence: The issue gives a complete C++ reproducer and a gdb backtrace ending in "#0  0x..in rmw_fastrtps_shared_cpp::__rmw_event_set_callback (rmw_event=0x5555559ea0b0, callback=0x0, user_data=0x0)" and "Thread 4 \"example_segfault\" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault." The Fast DDS maintainer diagnoses the cause and the rclcpp fix is merged -- https://github.com/ros2/rmw_fastrtps/issues/717

E2.evidence: Two separately built libraries: rclcpp (caller, through rcl and rmw_implementation) and rmw_fastrtps_shared_cpp (the rmw implementation). The failure is a call-ordering assumption across the rmw API: rclcpp clears the event callback after the event's parent publisher has been destroyed, and rmw_fastrtps shares one listener between the publisher and its events. "it seems to me the info structure is used after it was destroyed. This would mean there is a call to `rmw_event_set_callback` after the call to `rmw_destroy_publisher`." -- https://github.com/ros2/rmw_fastrtps/issues/717 ; "Both the `EventHandler` and its associated pubs/subs share the same underlying rmw event listener ... When a pub/sub is destroyed, that listener is destroyed. There is a data race when the `~EventHandlerBase` calls  `clear_on_ready_callback()`, since it wants to access the listener that could have already been destroyed, thus causing a segfault." -- https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/pull/2349. Timing (call order) crossing the boundary is an interface failure even though the resolving edit is inside rclcpp. Not deployment wiring, build, or firmware.

E3.evidence: PAIR: rclcpp's calls (rcl_event_set_callback -> rmw_event_set_callback on a publisher event) feed rmw_fastrtps_shared_cpp, which dereferences the listener of the already destroyed publisher. Reproducer: nodes with a SensorDataQoS publisher are created in a loop and added to an EventsExecutor spinning in another thread.

E4.evidence: Observed segmentation fault: "Thread 4 \"example_segfault\" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault." -- https://github.com/ros2/rmw_fastrtps/issues/717

failed_conditions.quote: Three lines after setting `info->deleted = true;` there is a `delete info;`, so it seems to me the info structure is used after it was destroyed. This would mean there is a call to `rmw_event_set_callback` after the call to `rmw_destroy_publisher`.

loudness_evidence: The only evidence is a runtime crash captured in gdb: "Thread 4 \"example_segfault\" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault." No build, connection, or activation diagnostic from existing tooling is shown. -- https://github.com/ros2/rmw_fastrtps/issues/717

resolution.summary: rclcpp: remove clear_on_ready_callback() from ~EventHandlerBase and call it in a new ~EventHandler destructor, which runs while the derived class still holds parent_handle_ (the publisher/subscription), so the rmw listener is still alive when rmw_event_set_callback(NULL) is called.
resolution.evidence: Merged to rolling (PR 2349, 411dbe82) after green CI and backported to iron (PR 2387, 7877358e). The PR author states "Even without being able to reproduce properly on rolling, I think this fix may be correct and could avoid future issues." -- https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/pull/2349. No source shows the reproducer running without the segfault on identified revisions.

notes: Eligibility judgment: the underlying mistake is C++ destruction order inside rclcpp (derived-class member parent_handle_ is destroyed before the base-class destructor body runs), which could be read as internal; it is treated as an interface failure because the effect is an rmw API call made after the parent entity was destroyed, i.e. a call-ordering assumption between rclcpp and the rmw implementation (the rmw header does not state a publisher/event lifetime rule; rmw.h only says of rmw_event_set_callback that "this function could be called by the user at any time"). Class `other` is used because no listed class covers a call-ordering/lifetime violation. The consumer reaches the rmw symbols through rcl (rcl_publisher_event_init, rcl_event_set_callback, rcl_event_fini, rcl_publisher_fini) and rmw_implementation; these pass-through layers are not treated as separate units of this composition. The title calls it a data race and the rclcpp PR calls it one (the last reference to the EventHandler may be dropped on the executor thread); CONCURRENT is a possible alternative reading of the operation. The reporter also reproduces on Galactic/Humble with the standalone irobot-ros/events-executor package; the humble backport PR 2388 was closed unmerged. The reporter's proof-of-concept fix in rmw_fastrtps (mauropasse/rmw_fastrtps@adf1aa7e52b9aea8c1b76886683ae5e663237b81) was described by its author as "not correct, was just for illustration purpuses".
